result.title: Instructions Before Actions: Prospective and Retrospective Language Supervision for Driving Vision-Language-Action Data
result.summary: Driving vision-language-action (VLA) models can accept navigation instructions, yet predicting a driver's trajectory does not establish that a model follows the instruction. We study how driving-language supervision is collected and evaluated, distinguishing prospective instructions issued before an action from retrospective labels written after observing it. We develop ADVLAT-Engine to synchronize spoken instructions, road-scene video, and vehicle trajectories, and compare three navigation apps on 48 replayed routes. On 87 maneuvers announced by both Google Maps and a passenger, the passenger uses more scene-dependent language. We evaluate four open driving VLAs before and after fine-tuning on prospective navigation-app drives. Fine-tuning reduces passenger-drive trajectory error by 23-59%, but instruction effects remain inconsistent. At real intersections, counterfactual instructions reveal stronger responsiveness: fine-tuned Alpamayo~2 Super gains 31 and 18 accuracy points at 15 and 5~m, while Qwen-Drive follows alternative maneuvers more reliably with a discrete command than with a sentence. We additionally collected retrospective annotations from four people for the driving recordings and describe controlled comparisons of annotation content, timing, and downstream learning; those analyses are pending. Our findings separate maneuver prediction from instruction-following and establish a framework for comparing prospective and retrospective supervision.

AI.brief_summary: 开发 ADVLAT-Engine 同步语音导航指令、道路视频与车辆轨迹，比较导航 app 与乘客在 48 条复现路线上的事前指令表述，并用真实路口反事实指令评测四个开源驾驶 VLA 的指令遵循；事后标注的对照分析尚未完成。
AI.relevance_reason: 工作把「预测轨迹」与「遵循指令」显式分开，用反事实指令检验模型是否真正使用语言与场景证据而非走捷径，与 LVR 关注的视觉旁路、贡献分配及前瞻/回溯式监督差异可供核查，但不涉及 latent 推理状态本身。
